method.role: viewer via the real product transaction and RLS
method.fixture: Explicitly approved synthetic fixtures only; this does not import or approve external material
method.timing: EXPLAIN ANALYZE instrumentation; not HTTP latency, throughput, model quality or a technology-stack comparison
method.cache: ANALYZE and product correctness calls precede EXPLAIN; warmed, not a cold-cache experiment
method.planner: Default planner settings; no forced indexes
method.concurrency: Other isolated tests may be running; no exclusive hardware claim
method.limits: Metadata is complete through 512 labels. Direct exact SQL is also measured at 4096; the template client still refuses that incomplete vocabulary.

SELECT f.id,f.subject,f.predicate,f.version,r.value,
      r.id AS revision_id,r.source_id
      FROM facts f LEFT JOIN revisions r ON r.id=f.current_revision_id AND r.project_id=f.project_id AND r.fact_id=f.id AND r.version=f.version
      WHERE f.project_id=$1 AND f.subject=$2 AND f.predicate=$3 AND f.version>0 LIMIT 2

queries.sql:
SELECT f.id AS fact_id,f.subject,f.predicate,
    r.id AS revision_id,r.version,r.value,r.created_at,r.approved_by,r.source_id,
    c.id AS candidate_id,c.expected_version,c.proposed_by,c.source_id AS candidate_source_id,
    c.subject AS candidate_subject,c.predicate AS candidate_predicate,c.value AS candidate_value,c.status AS candidate_status
    FROM unnest($2::int[],$3::int[]) WITH ORDINALITY AS requested(id,version,ordinal)
    LEFT JOIN facts f ON f.id=requested.id AND f.project_id=$1
    LEFT JOIN revisions r ON r.fact_id=f.id AND r.project_id=f.project_id AND r.version=requested.version
    LEFT JOIN candidates c ON c.id=r.candidate_id AND c.project_id=r.project_id
    ORDER BY requested.ordinal
